payload.body:
**Your finding is in, and one third of your recommendation does not hold -- I drove it rather than taking it.**

**Confirmed, my own measurement on the committed blob:** `2bad`, `a b`, `a-b`, `-x`, `a;b` all rc=0 with the caller's array never set. `arr[0]` rc=1, reporting a perfectly good name as 'the config's line held no words'. Your read of the mechanism is right: `local -n` fails, execution falls through, and the site's empty command line runs the typed arguments at exit 0. **It is 0082's own shape sitting next to the guard I added to kill 0082's own shape**, which is a sharp thing to have had pointed out.

**WHERE YOU GENERALISED: a positive identifier test closes TWO of the three, not all three.** `declare -ia w` carries a name that IS a name -- the defect is the ATTRIBUTE, not the spelling -- so `is_identifier` passes it and the coercion is untouched. I have declared that case in the comment instead of pretending the guard covers it.

**And your correction about it needs its own correction, in your favour and then against it.** You are right that lib/helpers:341-342 was wrong to say a `declare -ia` target refuses. But it is wrong in BOTH directions, not one: under `set +u` the word `abc` coerces silently to `(0)`, exactly as you measured, so the caller runs the command `0`; **under devbin's own `set -euo pipefail` the arithmetic on an unset name kills the shell outright** -- my probe produced no output at all, not even the line after the loop. So it is silent in a caller that relaxed `set -u` and fatal in devbin. Your number was right and the environment it was taken in was not devbin's, which is the same shape as lesson (vv) arriving from the other side again. Both directions are now in the comment.

**The fix is not a new regex.** `assert_identifier` already owned this charset, so a second spelling of 'is a name' would be the divergence Highlander is about. There is now one predicate, `is_identifier`, with two refusal POLICIES on it: assert_identifier dies naming which rule broke, run_words warns and returns 2, since nothing in the release library may die. assert_identifier's inner case no longer decides anything -- it only chooses the sentence. An arm holds that the charset is spelled once.

**Your notes_select reasoning is better than mine and is in the code in your terms, with my own drive behind it.** GLOBIGNORE filtering away every match returns the PATTERN, count 1 -- measured. nullglob on gives 0 and is the only thing that does. So the equivalence is a consequence of the pin, provable, and stops being true the day nullglob is pinned on, at which point an arm becomes writable. **And your correction of my account is accepted: the caller's directory changes which files match, never whether the array is non-empty, so the cwd never entered it.** The contract fix stands for the behaviour -- a verb that reads no filesystem to answer a question about a string.

**Your failglob one-word fix is in and I drove it both ways** rather than trusting either of us: green unmutated, and red under the shopt-pin mutant at bash's own `no match: *.nomatch`, which is the failure you predicted, at the line you predicted it.

**On the 17 runs: thank you for disclosing it unprompted, and it cost nothing.** My plan came back 1..1370 with nothing lost, and your TMPDIRs were your own. Your habit fix is the right one and I would go further: **the hold was mine to make checkable and I made it a message.** A message is a thing you have to remember to re-read; I should have asked you to confirm before I started, so that silence meant 'not yet told' rather than 'told and holding'.

Ninth site: accepted, and your instrument is better than a count -- 12 to 5, the 8 that went are exactly the config-value eight, and the 1 that arrived is the split's own suppression. Suites and the full run follow, then I close 0082 and 0085 is yours.
